entities.name: Yehuda HaKohen ben Meir
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Yehuda HaKohen ben Meir, also known as Yehudah Leontin, was a rabbi and Talmudic scholar of the late tenth and early eleventh century CE, born in the city of Meir, in the region of Ashkenaz, within the Holy Roman Empire.




He was a central figure in the development of Jewish law and theology, particularly in the areas of Halakha and Kabbalah, and played a key role in the creation of the Toledot Ha-Rabbonim, a comprehensive collection of biographies of prominent rabbis. His works, such as the Book of the Elders of Zikart and the Book of the Elders of Ashkenaz, were highly influential in shaping Jewish thought and practice.




He was succeeded by his son, Judah ben Meir, who continued his father's work and further developed his teachings. Yehuda ben Meir's legacy extends beyond the Jewish community, as his writings and ideas have had a lasting impact on Western philosophy and intellectual history.

A striking testament to his enduring influence is the continued study and reverence for his works in Jewish schools and communities around the world.
